Word experts agree that social media and politics have driven conversations that use these terms.
Here are their selections for Word of the Year.
The American Dictionary Publisher, Miriam Webster
Selected polarization as its word of the year for 2024.
The dictionary publisher defines polarization.
Division into two sharply distinct opposites.
especially a state in which the opinions, beliefs, or interests of a group or society
become concentrated at opposing extremes.
as divided as Americans appear.
Meriam Webster says, polarization happens to be one idea that both sides of the political spectrum agree on.
The word was widely used in news stories and broadcasts.
to describe the presidential election in the United States.
Supporters of both candidates, President-elect Donald Trump?
and Vice President Kamala Harris.
Voice the opinion that the opposing candidate...
was a threat to the nation.
The US election also brought attention to two other words.
Panda and Weird
Trump supporters accused Harris of pandering.
In other words,
Changing her policy positions to get votes.
Democratic Vice Presidential candidate Tim Walls
called his opponents, weird.
The editors at Britain's Oxford University Press say, usage of its word of the year selection.
increased by 230% from 2023 to 2024.
Oxford defines brain rot.
as the supposed deterioration of a person's mental or intellectual state.
especially viewed as the result of overconsumption of material.
Now, particularly online content.
Consider to be trivial or unchallenging.
The phrase likely first appeared in written form.
In Henry David Theroux's 1854 book, Walden.
about his experiences living a simple lifestyle.
while England endeavors to cure the potato rot.
will not any endeavor to cure the brain rot.
which prevails so much more widely and fatally.
In 2024, the phrase has been used to describe concerns about the harm of overconsuming.
or watching and reading too much online material.
Casper Graphwall, President of Oxford Languages noted.
I find it fascinating that the term brain rot has been adopted by Gen Z and Gen Alpha.
Those communities largely responsible for the use and creation of the digital content the term refers to.
